summary: A single Fedora 44 bootc image offering COSMIC as the full desktop and Hyprland as a tiling alternative, chosen at the greeter. Verdict: this co-installation is SANE and I verified it empirically — the research host is Fedora 44 (VERSION="44 (COSMIC)") running exactly this combination, with cosmic.desktop, hyprland.desktop and hyprland-uwsm.desktop all present in /usr/share/wayland-sessions and cosmic-greeter.service active as display-manager.service. The two stacks do not fight: portal preference is resolved per-session via XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP, so /usr/share/xdg-desktop-portal/cosmic-portals.conf ("default=cosmic;gtk;") and hyprland-portals.conf ("default=hyprland;gtk") coexist without either overriding the other, and both xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic and xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland install disjoint D-Bus names and .portal files. There is exactly ONE greeter, and cosmic-greeter is it — it is not a COSMIC-only display manager but a greetd greeter (it Requires: greetd, ships /etc/greetd/cosmic-greeter.toml with ExecStart=greetd --config, and its binary contains both "wayland-sessions" and "xsessions" enumeration strings), so it lists and launches Hyprland like any other session. The single genuine complication is that Hyprland is entirely absent from Fedora 44 and RPM Fusion — a batched repoquery over the whole Hyprland stack (hyprland, hyprpaper, hypridle, hyprlock, hyprpicker, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland, aquamarine, uwsm, hyprpolkitagent, rofi-wayland) returned only wlogout. The compositor must come from COPR, and that COPR necessarily *upgrades* Fedora's hyprutils/hyprlang/hyprgraphics/hyprcursor libraries, which is safe only because nothing outside the Hyprland stack consumes them (verified: --whatrequires on all four returns only their own -devel subpackages and each other; cosmic-comp and cosmic-session have zero hypr dependencies). This is a good image to bake precisely because Hyprland ships no default config at all and is unusable without one.

packages.name: cosmic-session
packages.why: COSMIC session entry point; ships /usr/share/wayland-sessions/cosmic.desktop and cosmic-session.target. Verified 1.4.0 in updates.

packages.name: cosmic-comp
packages.why: COSMIC Wayland compositor. Also a hard dependency of cosmic-greeter (which runs the greeter UI on top of it).

packages.name: cosmic-greeter
packages.why: THE greeter for the whole image. Despite the name it is a greetd greeter and enumerates /usr/share/wayland-sessions, so it launches Hyprland too. Aliased to display-manager.service.

packages.name: greetd
packages.why: Required by cosmic-greeter; the actual login daemon. cosmic-greeter.service literally execs 'greetd --config /etc/greetd/cosmic-greeter.toml'.

packages.name: greetd-selinux
packages.why: SELinux policy for greetd. Hard Requires of cosmic-greeter — omitting it breaks login on an enforcing bootc image.

unavailable.name: hyprland
unavailable.alternative: COPR. Verified absent from fedora, updates and both RPM Fusion repos. Use solopasha/hyprland (the widely-used, most complete Hyprland COPR) or lionheartp/Hyprland (what the research host runs, currently 0.56.0). NOT optional — this is the entire tiling half of the image.

unavailable.name: aquamarine
unavailable.alternative: COPR (same Hyprland COPR). Hyprland's backend/rendering library, hard Requires: aquamarine >= 0.9.2. Absent from Fedora entirely, so you cannot even rebuild Hyprland against Fedora libs without also building this.

unavailable.name: xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland
unavailable.alternative: COPR (same Hyprland COPR). Absolutely required — without it Hyprland has no screencast/screenshot and every Flatpak file chooser misbehaves. Ships /usr/share/xdg-desktop-portal/hyprland-portals.conf. Do NOT substitute xdg-desktop-portal-wlr (which IS in Fedora): it lacks Hyprland's window-picker and global shortcuts.

unavailable.name: hyprpaper
unavailable.alternative: Use swaybg (in Fedora, already in packages). Avoids a COPR package for zero functional loss.

unavailable.name: hypridle
unavailable.alternative: Use swayidle (in Fedora, already in packages), or take hypridle from the Hyprland COPR if you want hyprlock integration.

unavailable.name: hyprlock
unavailable.alternative: Use swaylock (in Fedora, already in packages), or hyprlock from the Hyprland COPR. swaylock is the lower-risk choice for an immutable image because its PAM config is Fedora-maintained.

unavailable.name: hyprpolkitagent
unavailable.alternative: Use mate-polkit (in Fedora, already in packages). polkit-gnome does NOT exist in Fedora 44 — verified absent — so do not reach for the usual muscle-memory package.

unavailable.name: hyprpicker
unavailable.alternative: COPR (Hyprland COPR). Colour picker. Optional; grim+slurp can approximate.

unavailable.name: hyprshot / grimblast
unavailable.alternative: COPR (lionheartp ships both; solopasha ships hyprland-contrib). Optional convenience wrappers — grim|slurp|swappy from Fedora already covers the functionality.

unavailable.name: hyprsunset
unavailable.alternative: Use gammastep or wlsunset (both verified in Fedora) for night-light under Hyprland.

unavailable.name: uwsm
unavailable.alternative: COPR only (lionheartp ships uwsm 0.26.4 plus hyprland-uwsm). Universal Wayland Session Manager — wraps the session in systemd user units. Recommended if you want Hyprland to get proper systemd session scoping like COSMIC has; adds a second wayland-session entry (hyprland-uwsm.desktop).

unavailable.name: rofi-wayland
unavailable.alternative: Use fuzzel (in Fedora, already in packages). Fedora's 'rofi' package is the X11 build — its deps include libxcb-ewmh/libxcb-xinerama/libxcb-icccm — so it is the wrong tool for a pure-Wayland image.

unavailable.name: polkit-gnome
unavailable.alternative: Does not exist in Fedora 44. Use mate-polkit or xfce-polkit (both verified present).

unavailable.name: nwg-look / nwg-displays
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora (only nwg-panel is). Use wdisplays for output layout and qt6ct/gtk settings via cosmic-settings. Or COPR solopasha/hyprland which carries the nwg-* family.

unavailable.name: swww
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora. Use swaybg for static wallpaper; swww only matters if you want animated transitions.

unavailable.name: ghostty / wezterm
unavailable.alternative: Neither is in Fedora 44. Use foot or kitty (both verified). ghostty is available via COPR pgdev/ghostty if specifically wanted.

unavailable.name: hyprland-qtutils
unavailable.alternative: COPR (Hyprland COPR). Provides Hyprland's Qt dialogs (update/error popups). Purely cosmetic; Hyprland logs to stderr without it.

copr: solopasha/hyprland — RECOMMENDED. The most complete and most widely used Hyprland COPR: hyprland, aquamarine, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland, hyprpaper, hypridle, hyprlock, hyprpicker, hyprpolkitagent, hyprland-qtutils, hyprland-plugins, hyprsunset, plus the nwg-* tooling. Pin with a versionlock or a dated snapshot in the Containerfile — it tracks upstream Hyprland aggressively and a rebuild can move you a minor version.

lionheartp/Hyprland — ALTERNATIVE, and what the Fedora 44 research host actually runs (hyprland 0.56.0, uwsm 0.26.4, hyprland-uwsm, aquamarine 0.13.0, hyprwire, hyprshot, grimblast, hdrop, gpu-screen-recorder). Choose this one if you want uwsm/systemd session integration, which solopasha does not ship. Caution: it also carries hyprland-git with dozens of snapshot builds — exclude that package name explicitly or dnf may prefer a git snapshot over the stable build.

external.name: Hyprland default configuration
external.method: Author it yourself and COPY it into the image at /etc/skel/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf. Hyprland ships NO default config — verified: the hyprland RPM installs only /usr/share/hypr/{hyprland.lua,wall*.png,lockdead*.png,stubs/} and no .conf anywhere. A user landing in a Hyprland session with no config gets a black screen with no keybinds and no way to open a terminal. This is the single most important file in the layer.

external.name: Waybar / mako / fuzzel default configs
external.method: COPY into /etc/skel/.config/{waybar,mako,fuzzel}/. Waybar with no config shows a mostly empty bar; mako and fuzzel have usable built-in defaults but look inconsistent with COSMIC's theme without one.

external.name: greetd session-wrapper hardening (optional)
external.method: Drop-in file, not an external RPM. If you adopt uwsm, add hyprland-uwsm.desktop's session as the preferred entry and consider hiding the plain hyprland.desktop with NoDisplay=true so the greeter shows one Hyprland option rather than two confusing ones.

integration.detail: systemctl enable cosmic-greeter.service. It carries [Install] Alias=display-manager.service, so enabling it wires up the whole login path. Do NOT also enable greetd.service or gdm.service — all three claim display-manager.service and the alias symlink will be won by whichever was enabled last, producing a nondeterministic image. Enable exactly one.

cosmic-greeter.service declares Conflicts=getty@tty1.service and After=plymouth-quit-wait.service, and its greetd config pins [terminal] vt="1". No manual VT juggling needed, but do not separately enable getty@tty1.

/etc/skel/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf — the load-bearing integration. Must at minimum set a monitor line, exec-once for waybar/mako/swaybg/mate-polkit/the portal, $mainMod binds for terminal (kitty or foot), fuzzel, and killactive, plus 'env = XCURSOR_SIZE,24'. Because the image is immutable, /etc/skel is the correct vehicle: it seeds only NEW users at useradd time and leaves existing users' configs alone, which is exactly the semantics you want. A system-wide /usr/share fallback is NOT a substitute here — Hyprland does not read one.

Portal preference needs NO intervention and you should resist the urge to add /etc/xdg-desktop-portal/portals.conf. Verified on a live system: cosmic-portals.conf ([preferred] default=cosmic;gtk;) and hyprland-portals.conf ([preferred] default=hyprland;gtk) coexist because xdg-desktop-portal selects <lowercased XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP>-portals.conf at runtime. cosmic.desktop sets DesktopNames=COSMIC and hyprland.desktop sets DesktopNames=Hyprland, so each session resolves to its own backend. A hand-written global portals.conf would override BOTH and break one of the two sessions.

exec-once=/usr/libexec/xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland is generally unnecessary (D-Bus activation handles it), but DO exec-once a polkit agent (/usr/libexec/mate-polkit/polkit-mate-authentication-agent-1) — nothing autostarts it under Hyprland, and without it every privileged GUI action silently fails.

cosmic-greeter Requires group(video) and user(cosmic-greeter), created via /usr/lib/sysusers.d/cosmic-greeter.conf. In a bootc build, confirm systemd-sysusers actually ran at build time — if the cosmic-greeter user is missing at first boot the greeter fails to start and you get no login at all. Verify with `getent passwd cosmic-greeter` in the Containerfile.

Install greetd-selinux (it is a hard Requires of cosmic-greeter, so dnf pulls it, but state it explicitly). Also run a relabel or ensure /etc/greetd and /etc/skel content carry correct contexts — mislabeled greeter config is a classic cause of a bootc image that boots to a blank tty under enforcing.

cosmic-greeter ships /etc/pam.d/cosmic-greeter and Requires fprintd-pam. If the image has no fingerprint hardware this is harmless, but the PAM stack pulls fprintd in — accept it or the greeter package will not install.

Hyprland launched from a greetd greeter does NOT get a systemd user session scope the way cosmic-session does (cosmic-session ships cosmic-session.target). If you want systemd-managed user services under Hyprland, adopt uwsm from the lionheartp COPR and prefer hyprland-uwsm.desktop; otherwise put everything in exec-once.

COPR library override is REQUIRED and is safe. Fedora 44 ships hyprutils 0.7.1 / hyprlang 0.6.4 / hyprgraphics 0.1.5 / hyprcursor 0.1.11, but hyprland 0.56 Requires hyprutils >= 0.8.4 and hyprgraphics >= 0.1.6, so the COPR versions (hyprutils 0.14.0, hyprgraphics 0.5.1) must win. Soname bumps are real (libhyprutils.so.6 -> .so.13, libhyprgraphics.so.0 -> .so.4) but harmless: --whatrequires on all four Fedora packages returns only their own -devel subpackages and each other, and cosmic-comp/cosmic-session have zero hypr dependencies. Nothing in COSMIC breaks.

Skip the @cosmic-desktop group and list packages explicitly. Verified group contents are thin and partly wrong for this image: mandatory = cosmic-edit, cosmic-files, cosmic-session, cosmic-store, cosmic-term; default = cosmic-initial-setup, cosmic-player, flatpak, gnome-keyring-pam, system-config-printer, toolbox. It pulls flatpak/system-config-printer (your desktop-common layer's job) and, critically, does NOT include cosmic-greeter, cosmic-settings, cosmic-panel or the applets. Installing the group alone gives you a COSMIC image with no greeter and no settings app.

Avoid @cosmic-desktop-apps entirely. Verified contents: ark, gnome-calculator, gnome-disk-utility, gnome-system-monitor, nheko, okular, rhythmbox, thunderbird. That drags in KDE and GNOME app stacks plus a Matrix client and a mail client — hundreds of MB of unrelated dependencies that belong nowhere near a DE layer.

services: cosmic-greeter.service — enable this one and only this one; it aliases display-manager.service
cosmic-greeter-daemon.service — pulled in via Wants= by cosmic-greeter.service; no separate enable needed but verify the symlink exists in the built image
systemd-sysusers — must run at build time to create the cosmic-greeter user from /usr/lib/sysusers.d/cosmic-greeter.conf
DO NOT enable: greetd.service, gdm.service, sddm.service — they contend for the display-manager.service alias
risks: GREETER RECOMMENDATION: use cosmic-greeter. Reasoning, from direct inspection rather than assumption — cosmic-greeter is NOT a COSMIC-only display manager, it is a greetd greeter (Requires: greetd + greetd-selinux, ships /etc/greetd/cosmic-greeter.toml whose default_session command is cosmic-greeter-start, and its service unit execs `greetd --config`). Its binary contains both 'wayland-sessions' and 'xsessions' enumeration strings, so it lists every session desktop file including Hyprland's. The research host proves it end-to-end: cosmic-greeter.service is the active display-manager with cosmic.desktop, hyprland.desktop and hyprland-uwsm.desktop all offered. It gives you greetd's simplicity, a graphical session picker, per-user session memory, and it is already a mandatory dependency chain of the COSMIC half. gdm is the wrong choice: it drags the entire GNOME session stack, xdg-desktop-portal-gnome, and gnome-shell into a DE layer that is supposed to contain neither DE, and it sets XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP in ways that have historically confused non-GNOME sessions. greetd+tuigreet is a downgrade, not an upgrade: it is the same greetd daemon underneath, but a TUI picker on a machine whose flagship session is a polished GTK desktop is an aesthetic regression for zero benefit, and you would still need to install cosmic-greeter's dependencies anyway. Choose cosmic-greeter; keep tuigreet installed as a fallback only if you want a recovery login path.

COSMIC MATURITY — better than its reputation but not GNOME/KDE-stable. Fedora 44 ships COSMIC 1.4.0 in updates (1.0.9 in GA), i.e. post-1.0 stable releases, and Fedora 44's own VERSION string is '44 (COSMIC)', signalling first-class distro support. That said, COSMIC 1.x is roughly a year old as a stable line: accessibility (screen reader / AT-SPI) is markedly behind GNOME, the settings app still has gaps, third-party theming is immature, and cosmic-store is a thinner Flatpak frontend than GNOME Software. Acceptable as a daily driver, not yet appropriate for a deployment with hard a11y requirements.

HYPRLAND + IMAGENOLOGY (medical/diagnostic imaging) — this is the one place I would say plainly: do not use Hyprland as the session for image interpretation. Hyprland has no colour management protocol support of the kind that matters here — no ICC profile application, no wp_color_management_v1 maturity, no calibrated output path — so pixel values are displayed uncorrected and are not diagnostically trustworthy. Its fractional scaling is also the classic wlroots-style approach (render at integer scale, downscale), which resamples and can introduce interpolation artefacts on fine structures; that is exactly the failure mode you cannot tolerate when reading images. COSMIC (via cosmic-comp/cosmic-randr) has substantially better display-configuration and scaling handling and is the session that should be used for any actual imaging work. Ship Hyprland as the productivity/tiling session by all means — just do not let it be the one anyone reads a study on. If imaging is the primary purpose of this image, consider whether the Hyprland half earns its ~15 packages plus a COPR dependency at all.

COPR SUPPLY-CHAIN — Hyprland cannot come from Fedora, so the image's tiling half depends on a single unofficial COPR maintained by one person, with no Fedora security-response SLA and no guarantee of a rebuild after a Fedora mass rebuild. Mitigate by pinning: use `dnf install hyprland-0.56.0` style version pins or a dated COPR snapshot repo URL in the Containerfile, so an image rebuild is reproducible and a broken upstream release cannot silently land in production.

hyprland-git TRAP in the lionheartp COPR — that repo carries dozens of hyprland-git snapshot builds (0.55.4^51.git… through ^69.git… and beyond) alongside stable hyprland. Depending on version comparison, dnf may resolve to a git snapshot. Explicitly `--exclude=hyprland-git` or install the fully-versioned stable NEVRA.

TWO NOTIFICATION DAEMONS, TWO IDLE DAEMONS, TWO WALLPAPER DAEMONS in one image (cosmic-notifications/mako, cosmic-idle/swayidle, cosmic-bg/swaybg). Harmless as long as each is started only by its own session — COSMIC starts its set via cosmic-session, and the Hyprland set must be started ONLY from exec-once in hyprland.conf. Never put mako/swaybg/swayidle into a systemd user unit with WantedBy=default.target, or they will start inside the COSMIC session too and you will get duplicate notifications and a wallpaper fight.

/etc/skel SEEDS ONLY NEW USERS. On a bootc image the /etc/skel Hyprland config reaches users created after the image is deployed. An existing user upgrading to a new image build gets NO config update — and if you later fix a broken default keybind, existing users keep the broken one. Document this, or ship the config as a versioned file the user's config `source=`s from /usr/share so you retain the ability to push fixes.

IMAGE SIZE / SCOPE — resist installing @cosmic-desktop or @cosmic-desktop-apps as a shortcut; the latter alone pulls ark, okular, nheko, rhythmbox and thunderbird, mixing KDE and GNOME app stacks into a DE layer.

Fedora's `rofi` is the X11 build (deps include libxcb-ewmh, libxcb-xinerama, libxcb-icccm) and rofi-wayland does not exist in Fedora 44. If a copied upstream Hyprland config references rofi, it will run through XWayland with degraded behaviour. Standardise on fuzzel and adjust the shipped config accordingly.
notes: desktop-common (excluded here per instructions, but these are the ones this layer genuinely assumes exist there): pipewire + wireplumber (screencast portals on BOTH sessions are useless without them), xdg-desktop-portal itself (the frontend — both cosmic and hyprland backends Require it), flatpak, fonts, mesa/vulkan drivers, and NetworkManager. If desktop-common does not carry xdg-desktop-portal and pipewire, screen sharing silently fails in both sessions and it is very hard to debug.

xdg-desktop-portal-gtk is worth putting in desktop-common rather than here: BOTH cosmic-portals.conf and hyprland-portals.conf name `gtk` as their fallback backend, so it is a shared requirement of the two sessions, not a property of either.

gnome-keyring/gnome-keyring-pam are arguably desktop-common too — I listed them here because cosmic-portals.conf names gnome-keyring explicitly for the Secret portal and Hyprland has no alternative, so this layer breaks without them.

OPEN QUESTION — uwsm or not? It is the difference between Hyprland getting a real systemd user session (like cosmic-session.target gives COSMIC) versus a bare exec-once soup. uwsm exists only in lionheartp's COPR, not solopasha's, so the answer determines which COPR you pick. My lean: if you want the two sessions to behave consistently for systemd user services, take lionheartp + uwsm and hide the non-uwsm hyprland.desktop.

OPEN QUESTION — is the Hyprland session actually wanted given the imagenology purpose? Given the colour-management and fractional-scaling findings above, the honest recommendation is COSMIC-primary, Hyprland-as-a-convenience. If nobody will use the tiling session for real work, dropping it removes an entire COPR dependency and about 15 packages from the trusted computing base.

VERIFICATION NOTE — all names under `packages` were echoed back by batched `dnf repoquery --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=fedora --enablerepo=updates --enablerepo=rpmfusion-*`. The Hyprland stack was checked in one batch (hyprland, hyprpaper, hypridle, hyprlock, hyprpicker, hyprshot, hyprsunset, hyprpolkitagent, hyprland-qtutils, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland, aquamarine, uwsm, rofi-wayland, polkit-gnome, wezterm, ghostty, nwg-look, nwg-displays, swww, wlogout, grimblast, hyprwire, hyprland-plugins) and returned exactly one result: wlogout. Group contents came from `dnf group info`, not from memory.
size_note: Roughly 1.2–1.8 GB installed for this layer alone, on top of fedora-bootc and desktop-common. The COSMIC half dominates at approximately 900 MB–1.2 GB: these are Rust binaries that statically link most of their crate graph, so each cosmic-* package is tens of MB with little sharing between them (cosmic-settings, cosmic-store, cosmic-files and cosmic-edit are the largest single contributors), plus cosmic-wallpapers which is pure image data and can be dropped to save on the order of 100–200 MB if you ship your own branding. The Hyprland half is comparatively cheap, roughly 150–250 MB including the COPR-supplied hyprland, aquamarine and portal, since waybar/fuzzel/mako/grim/slurp/swaybg/swayidle are all small C binaries in the single-digit MB range. Supporting bits (Xwayland, qt6-qtwayland, gnome-keyring, mate-polkit, blueman, adw-gtk3-theme) add roughly 150–250 MB, with qt6-qtwayland pulling the Qt6 base libraries being the notable lump. Two easy wins: exclude the debuginfo/debugsource packages the Hyprland COPRs publish (they are numerous and large), and skip @cosmic-desktop-apps, which would otherwise add ark, okular, nheko, rhythmbox and thunderbird along with the KDE and GNOME library stacks behind them — comfortably another 800 MB+ for applications unrelated to the desktop layer.
flatpaks: Nothing in this layer should be a Flatpak — compositors, greeters, portals and status bars are all system components that must be baked. Flatpak is the right mechanism for the *applications* the excluded @cosmic-desktop-apps group would have pulled in.
org.mozilla.firefox — if a browser is wanted, Flatpak it rather than adding thunderbird/firefox RPMs to a DE layer.
com.github.tchx84.Flatseal — genuinely useful on an immutable image for managing the Flatpak permissions that portals mediate; pairs directly with the portal work in this layer.
org.gnome.Calculator, org.gnome.SystemMonitor — Flatpak substitutes for the @cosmic-desktop-apps members, keeping GNOME libraries out of the image.
